children: On his birthday, Premier Energies' Group CFO reflects on three decades in finance, a landmark IPO, and why he still calls himself a student
Today, Nand Kishore Khandelwal turns 57. Ask him what he's proudest of after more than three decades in finance, and he won't point to a title or a trophy.
“My favourite milestone is not really an award or a designation,”
he says.
“It is having grown from a finance professional into a business leader, while still remaining a student of the profession.”
That sentence is as close as anyone will get to a mission statement for his career.

Khandelwal qualified as a Chartered Accountant in 1992, back when the job of a CFO began and ended with the ledger. He has spent the more than three decades since quietly proving that definition wrong, moving from pure accounting and control into strategy, technology and full business leadership. His early years were spent inside the finance functions of Param Industries, Dukes Products and Alumeco India Extrusion — companies where he learned, the hard way, that financial health is not just what shows up on a balance sheet but a discipline that touches every part of a business.

By the time he became CFO and President–Corporate Resources at Pitti Engineering in 2016, he was no longer just managing numbers — he was shaping strategy, structuring capital, and building the kind of high-performance finance systems that let a manufacturing business scale with confidence. He held that role for six years, through some of Pitti's most significant growth phases.

Then, in September 2023, came the assignment that would come to define this decade of his career: Group CFO of Premier Energies, the Hyderabad-based integrated solar cell and module manufacturer racing to meet India's renewable energy ambitions.

Less than a year into the job, Khandelwal was steering the company's finance function through one of the most closely watched public listings of 2024 — a Rs 2,830 crore IPO that closed nearly 75 times oversubscribed and listed with a gain of roughly 120 percent, pushing Premier Energies' market capitalisation past Rs 44,500 crore on debut. For a CFO, an IPO is not a ceremony — it is months of governance, disclosure, capital structuring and investor scrutiny compressed into a single moment where every number has to hold. That Khandelwal delivered it within a year of joining says as much about his preparation as it does about the company's promise.
It is exactly this arc — from custodian of the books to architect of the business — that he describes as the defining shift of his profession.
“The CFO's role has moved from being the custodian of numbers to becoming a partner in shaping the future of the business,”
he says of his journey.
“I have been fortunate to experience that transformation firsthand and contribute to businesses through different stages of their growth.”

The recognition has followed the work rather than led it. He has been named among Asia's 100 Power Leaders in Finance by White Page International, and more recently, CII's CFO of the Year for the Energy, Infrastructure & Utilities sector — a fitting honour for a finance leader whose current chapter is being written at the heart of India's solar manufacturing story, in a sector where capital discipline and technical credibility both matter as much as ambition.
Even now, with a successful listing behind him, Khandelwal isn't slowing down. Asked about the year ahead, his answer is characteristically unglamorous and precise:

“My focus is to help build a finance function that is ready for the next scale of the organisation — strong on governance and controls, but equally strong on technology, analytics and business partnership.”
And then, almost as an aside that reveals more than the rest of the answer combined:
“Personally, I also want to spend more time mentoring the next generation of finance leaders and sharing what I have learnt over the years.”

That instinct to teach, rather than simply lead, is perhaps the truest measure of the man behind the milestones. It shows up again in the advice he offers young professionals standing where he once stood:
“Don't build your career around titles; build it around learning and responsibility. Understand the business behind the numbers, stay curious about technology, and never compromise on integrity.”
And then, the line that could sit above his own career like a headline:
“Careers rarely unfold exactly as we plan them, but commitment has a remarkable way of creating the next opportunity.”

Three decades, five companies, one listing that made headlines, and a professional philosophy that hasn't wavered since 1992 — that is the story of Nand Kishore Khandelwal at 57. Not a finance leader who has arrived, but one who is, by his own description, still a student.
Happy birthday, Nand Kishore — here's to a year of building the next scale, and shaping the next generation.
Savi Khanna
BW Reporters Assistant Editor, BW Businessworld
